newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's GITIC Enterprises makes dazzling debut.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's GITIC Enterprises makes dazzling debut.

text.p: Shares in GITIC Enterprises Ltd, Hong Kong's most popular public offering on record, surged on their debut on the local bourse on Wednesday, ending up more than four times above their issue price.

The issue's small size, a heavy subscription response and hopes for future asset injections drove the shares to a HK$4.375 (56.5 U.S. cents) close, compared to the offer's HK$1.05 issue price, brokers said.
The shares, which topped the list of most actively traded stocks in value terms, hit a high of HK$5.15 after making their debut at HK$4.50. Their low was HK$4.25.
Volume was 153.1 million shares worth HK$704.6 million.
"The performance was stronger than we generally expected," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities.
The counter surged despite weakness in the overall market. The blue-chip Hang Seng index slipped 56.14 points to 12,776.39.
Analysts said many investors who failed to subscribe for the shares during the firm's initial public offering (IPO), were seen rushing in to buy.
The relatively small issue size and high subscription level had made the issue particularly hot, they said.

"Anticipation of room on the upside on hopes of future asset injections (by its China-based parent) also fueled follow-through buying," Kwong said. "However, the shares were seen capped at its high of HK$5.15 after the sharp rally."
GITIC Enterprises imports and sells construction materials in Hong Kong and China, and also owns the second floor of a shopping mall at GITIC Plaza in Guangzhou.

The company is indirectly controlled by the Guangdong provincial government's investment arm, Guangdong International Trust and Investment Corp (GITIC), which had total assets of about 20.56 billion yuan at the end of 1995.

GITIC Enterprises offered 100 million new shares at HK$1.05 each in its IPO, of which the 90 million shares available for public subscription were 892 times subscribed -- Hong Kong's most popular-ever IPO in terms of subscription level.
That broke the record set by carmaker Denway Investment Ltd in February 1993. Its 330 million-share issue was 657 times oversubscribed.
Analysts said a high grey market price of about HK$3.60 before the debut also helped lift the GITIC shares.

"The strong earnings outlook, after taking into account an expected huge exceptional gain due to interest income from the subscription monies, also gave investors a positive sign to buy," said Henri Lui, analyst at Mansion House.
Analysts estimate the interest income would be over HK$40 million, almost equal to the company's own earnings forecast of over HK$41 million for the year ended December 1996.

"Its earnings outlook is also seen bright on expectation of increasing demand for granite and marble products from the local office and hotel property developments," Lui said. "There are not many suppliers of these kinds of materials in Hong Kong."
Analysts said the next move of the stock would depend on the company's asset injection plans.

The shares surged despite market talk last week that the offering had hit a snag because GITIC might not have obtained all necessary approvals for the float from Chinese authorities. GITIC Enterprises later announced that the IPO and listing would proceed as scheduled, but it did not clarify the rumours in its statement last week.
Analysts said the confusion could cool down the speculative fever for China-related shares.
